one_line: A Hebrew parenting-advice talking head, posted before Passover 2023, listing 4 things parents should stop doing if they want a child who helps clean the house, with numbered on-screen badges, burned-in captions and two short acted-out kitchen skits.

hook.visual: Woman in a light pink blouse and jeans stands in a kitchen mid-sentence with hands moving. Behind her a boy in a dark T-shirt wipes a fridge with a purple cloth (2-6 s). A white text box sits top-left, a white strip with a pink word near the bottom and a big pink numeral 4 bottom-right.
hook.on_screen_text: רוצים לגדל ילד שתורם לניקיון הבית (Want to raise a child who contributes to cleaning the house) + דברים שאתם חייבים להפסיק לעשות, with להפסיק in pink and a large pink 4 (4 things you must stop doing)
hook.first_spoken_line: Whisper: ארבעה דברים שאתם חייבים להפסיק לעשות אם אתם רוצים לגדל ילד שתורם לניקיון הבית (Four things you must stop doing if you want to raise a child who contributes to cleaning the house)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Names a desirable outcome (a kid who helps at home) and a numbered list of 'stop doing' mistakes in the first frame, in a season when every parent is about to clean for Passover (caption plus upload date 2023-03-23). A real child visibly cleaning in the background makes the outcome look achievable (inferred).

beats.observed: Presenter in kitchen, boy cleaning the fridge behind her, hand gestures, text box plus pink numeral 4 held on screen the whole time.
beats.spoken: Whisper: four things you must stop doing if you want a child who contributes to cleaning the house.
beats.on_screen_text: רוצים לגדל ילד שתורם לניקיון הבית (Want to raise a child who contributes to cleaning the house) / דברים שאתם חייבים להפסיק לעשות (things you must stop doing) / big 4

beats.observed: Cut to a tight selfie-style close-up, a pink #1 badge, a black label strip and two-line white subtitles that change every 2 s.
beats.spoken: Whisper: kids watch us and want to help, they want to polish windows and wash floors; it is only us, constantly rushing through a million tasks, who put the brakes on them.
beats.on_screen_text: שימו את הרצון לתקתק בצד (Put the urge to rush things aside) / הילדים שלנו רואים אותנו (Our kids see us) / והם רוצים לעזור אם רוצים להבריק (and they want to help, if they want to polish) / ... ושמים להם ברקס! (and we put the brakes on them!)

beats.observed: Cut to a wider kitchen shot. She leans over with open hands, acting out a scene. No child is visible in these frames. A white sticker appears at 24 s.
beats.spoken: Whisper (medium reliability, two voices): an offer to show 'how', then a protest ('look at me'), then 'not like that'.
beats.on_screen_text: לא ככה עושים! (That's not how it's done!)

beats.observed: Wider framing, pink #2 badge, black label strip. Four 'yes, we do X' subtitle lines build up to a bold 'but' line.
beats.spoken: Whisper: step out of the quality-inspector role; yes we have more cleaning experience, yes we do it better, yes we want to help and teach them, but along the way the criticism only hurts their motivation.
beats.on_screen_text: צאו מתפקיד מבקר האיכות (Step out of the quality-inspector role) / נכון יש לנו יותר ניסיון בניקיון (True, we have more cleaning experience) / נכון אנחנו עושים את זה טוב יותר (True, we do it better) / נכון אנחנו בסה"כ רוצים לעזור (True, we only want to help) / להם ללמד אותם (teach them) / אבל בדרך הביקורת הזו רק פוגעת (but along the way this criticism only hurts)

beats.observed: New framing in a different part of the kitchen, pink #3 badge. At 48 s a quote box appears with the word תמיד in pink-red.
beats.spoken: Whisper: avoid generalisations and extreme words, e.g. 'you are so messy', 'you never bring the plate', 'you always forget the bag at the entrance'.
beats.on_screen_text: די להכללות! (Enough with generalisations!) / במוטיבציה שלהם (their motivation) / "אתה תמיד שוכח את התיק בכניסה" (You ALWAYS forget the bag at the entrance)

beats.observed: Third location (open living area). Speech bubble plus three stacked white cards, then subtitles that spell out a full example sentence.
beats.spoken: Whisper: instead, speak with an 'I' message: what I see, what I feel, what I need. Example with a child called Shira: I see your bag at the entrance, I worry someone could trip and fall, so please put it in your room or the closet.
beats.on_screen_text: במקום זה תדברי איתם מסר (Instead, speak to them with a message) / מסר ה"אני" (The 'I' message) / מה אני רואה? מה אני מרגישה? מה אני צריכה? (What do I see? What do I feel? What do I need?) / לדוגמא "שירה שלי אני רואה (For example, 'My Shira, I see') / שהתיק שלך בכניסה לבית אני דואגת (that your bag is at the entrance, I worry) / מישהו יכול להיתקל בו וליפול ולכן (someone could trip on it and fall, so) / בבקשה שימי אותו בחדר או הארון (please put it in the room or the closet)

beats.observed: Cutaway skit: she stands over the boy (dark T-shirt) at the counter by the fridge in a stern pose; a rotated sticker and a white box appear; the boy raises a hand to his forehead as if saluting.
beats.spoken: Whisper: a command to put dishes in the dishwasher and 'yes, commander'.
beats.on_screen_text: יונתן תכניס כלים למדיח! (Yonatan, put dishes in the dishwasher!) / כן המפקדת!! (Yes, commander!!)

beats.observed: Back to the living-area framing. Pink #4 badge appears faint, then fades. Subtitles continue to the last frame at 86 s; no sign-off, no end card visible.
beats.spoken: Whisper: nobody likes being talked down to, let alone ordered around; instead create a family conversation, share the list of pre-Passover chores, and let each person rank every chore by what they like and choose which to do.
beats.on_screen_text: אל תקחי את תפקיד המפקדת (Don't take the commander role) / אף אחד לא אוהב שמדברים אליו מגבוה (Nobody likes being spoken to from above) / ובטח שלא מורידים אליו פקודה (let alone being ordered) / במקום זה תייצרו שיח משפחתי (Instead create a family conversation) / את רשימת המטלות שיש לעשות לפני פסח (the list of chores to do before Passover) / שכל אחד ידרג כל מטלה לפי מה שהוא אוהב (everyone ranks each chore by what they like)

payoff: Each item pairs a mistake with a replacement behaviour. The most usable take-home, the 'I' message formula with a full example sentence, arrives at 50-66 s, and the family chore-ranking idea arrives at 76-87 s, so a viewer must stay almost the whole 87 s for item 4.
cta: none in the video (last frame is mid-explanation) and none in the caption, which ends with hashtags.
share_or_comment_trigger: Parents recognise themselves in the 'quality inspector' and 'commander' habits and the pre-Passover timing makes it easy to send to a partner. The 'I' message sentence is save-worthy. Only 79 comments (about 0.02% of views), so saves and shares are the likely behaviour, not debate (inferred; saves and shares are not in meta.json).
why_it_worked: 391,224 views is 21.9x the account median of 17,873, on a seasonal topic (caption: cleaning for Passover; uploaded 2023-03-23).
A numbered list with on-screen badges (4, #1, 2, 3, 4) plus a ready-to-say script inside the items gives viewers a reason to stay through 87 s, and the last item is held until about 72 s.
Like rate 0.85% is healthy but not exceptional and comments are few, so reach looks driven by topic, timing and list structure rather than controversy (inferred).
paid_signal: no: like rate 0.85% is well above the 0.3% level that suggests paid reach, and nothing in the frames or caption is promotional.

solo_route.how: 1) Barter with a child-development or parenting counsellor and agree one topic LumeBook can own (for example reading with a child), with 4 'stop doing' items; you write the skeleton and one ready-to-say sentence per item, they record a 60-80 s talking head on a phone in their own space. 2) Edit in CapCut: burned-in Hebrew subtitles, a black label strip per item, a big pink numeral badge 1 to 4, one white card per script line, and a red highlight on the 'always/never' word. 3) For the skit cutaways, either have the expert act both voices as in 21-24 s, or use a relative's child only with written parental consent. 4) End on the single most quotable script line, as the original does, with no hard CTA.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who puts their name on the advice, because the credibility is the whole format and a 24-year-old with no kids cannot be the advice-giver. Optional: parental consent if any child appears on camera.

lumebook_version.hook_he: 4 דברים שאתם חייבים להפסיק לעשות אם אתם רוצים ילד שאוהב ספרים
lumebook_version.concept: A barter expert names 4 habits that quietly turn story time into a chore (topics are placeholders for the expert to confirm), each with one sentence a parent can say tonight. LumeBook appears only at the end as a way to make the child the hero of the story; the advice itself must come from the expert, not from LumeBook.

evidence_notes: Observed: all on-screen Hebrew was read from frames (sheets 1-8 plus single frames at 0, 22 and 66 s). Spoken: Whisper Hebrew is good and tracks the burned-in subtitles, with some mishearings (for example 'לטקטק' for on-screen 'לתקתק', and a line at 69-71 s about 'Shira' being asked to share the house that is not on screen). Inferred: that the presenter is the account owner and a parenting professional (account name 'הורות פרקטית - הודיה טיבר' suggests it, but no credentials appear on screen), and that the boy is her child (not stated). The numeral on the #4 badge fades at 72-76 s. Saves and shares are not available. Duration 87.3 s per frames/index.json.
